sentences.text: Doliodus was an extinct cartilaginous fish, a member of the group Chondrichthyes, that lived during the Early Devonian period.

Its teeth featured two large pointed cusps separated by smaller projections called cusplets, and the animal possessed heterodont dentition, meaning it had two separate types of teeth in different regions of its mouth.

The best-preserved specimen shows a head and body measuring 23 cm long, with an estimated total length ranging from 50 to 75 cm, while its pectoral spines reached lengths of 5.5 cm, with isolated examples growing up to 9 cm.
The genus name Doliodus means 'to trick or deceive' because its tooth crowns closely resemble those of the unrelated genus Diplodus.
The species was originally known only from isolated teeth and fin spines before a well-preserved body fossil was later assigned to it.
Joseph Whiteaves first identified the material in 1881, naming it Ctenacanthus latispinosus based on isolated fin spines, though the genus Doliodus itself was not named until Traquair did so in 1893.

In 2003, Randall Miller and coauthors assigned a well-preserved fossil specimen, catalogued as NBMG 10127, to the species Doliodus problematicus, with all known material originating from the Campbellton Formation in Campbellton, New Brunswick.
Some authors suggest the cartilaginous skeleton of Doliodus may have been reinforced by mineralized tessellations, though this hypothesis is considered uncertain.

Since the discovery of a more complete specimen, Doliodus has been classified as a member of the family Omalodontidae and order Omalodontiformes, and it is generally believed to be part of the stem-group of Chondrichthyes, having diverged earlier than the two living subclasses.
However, some authors consider Doliodus to have an uncertain position within Chondrichthyes and have not assigned it to a specific order or family.
Doliodus lived during the Emsian stage of the Early Devonian, approximately 409 to 397 million years ago, with specific dating placing the stage between 410.62 and 393.47 million years ago.
It is debated whether non-tooth material belongs to Doliodus; some researchers include it in D. latispinosus, while others restrict the genus to only teeth of D. problematicus.
Michal Ginter suggests the articulated material and fin spines may belong to the genus Portalodus or an unnamed intermediate genus, tentatively naming it Portalodus? latispinosus.
